evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:687 — exchange_code_for_tokens() builds `reqwest::Client::new()` with no .timeout(); the SSO callback awaits the PM OAuth token endpoint with no upper bound
backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:711 — get_user_info() same pattern: `reqwest::Client::new()`, unbounded .get(pm_userinfo_url) on the login/exchange/sync paths

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:748 — introspect_pm_token() same pattern: `reqwest::Client::new()`, unbounded .post(pm_introspect_url); reached by sso_callback, exchange_pm_token, create_mobile_sso_token, sync_session

Contrast: state.rs:757 PmApiClient correctly uses reqwest::Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(..)); the SSO path is the only outbound HTTP without a deadline. A slow/hung PM server stalls SSO request tasks indefinitely (reqwest default = no timeout), a resource-exhaustion vector on the auth-critical path. Each call also allocates a fresh Client per request, defeating connection/TLS pooling
Fix: add .timeout(...)/.connect_timeout(...) (or reuse a single pooled client stored on AppState) for the three SSO reqwest clients
